"d222cce5-96b3-53b1-84ca-5d6ee64c9788" :question/id #uuid "d222cce5-96b3-53b1-84ca-5d6ee64c9788"] [:db/add "d222cce5-96b3-53b1-84ca-5d6ee64c9788" :question/problem "Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y-4z &=4 \\ -x+y &=4 \\ 2x-6z &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$."] [:db/add "d222cce5-96b3-53b1-84ca-5d6ee64c9788" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -2 & -4 & 4 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & -6 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & -6 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 2 & 0 & -6 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-3 \\ y &=1-(-1)(-3) \\ &=-2 \\ x &=2-(-1)(-2) \\ &\quad -(-2)(-3) \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-6,-2,-3\right)
$$

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -6 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 6 & -1 & 7 \\ 2 & -9 & 1 & -7\end{array}\right]

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -6 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 6 & -1 & 7 \\ 2 & -9 & 1 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 6 & -1 & 7 \\ 2 & -9 & 1 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 9 \\ 2 & -9 & 1 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 9 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-3 \\ y &=3-(-1)(-3) \\ &=0 \\ x &=1-(-3)(0) \\ &\quad -(-1)(-3) \\ &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-2,0,-3\right)
$$

$$

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -6\end{array}\right]

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-2 \\ y &=5-(-2)(-2) \\ &=1 \\ x &=4-(-2)(1) \\ &\quad -(-2)(-2) \\ &=2\end{aligned}

\left(-2,0,-3\right)
